Everett Jackson

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 30, Dallas County, Texas · Open seat

Small business owner and community organizer

Everett Jackson is a Republican small business owner and community organizer from Dallas who has not held public office before. He finished in the top two of the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Texas' 30th Congressional District and went to a May 26 runoff against Sholdon Daniels. News coverage from September and October 2026 names him as the Republican nominee facing Democrat Frederick D. Haynes III for the seat now held by Rep. Jasmine Crockett.

Where Jackson stands

Economy and jobs
Says he supports job growth.
National security / drug cartels
Supports strengthening national security against drug cartels.
Religious freedom
Says he supports protecting religious freedom.
Child tax credit
Supports increasing the child tax credit.
Federal spending
Calls for making the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) spending cuts permanent.
Election administration
Says Friendship-West Baptist Church should not be a polling place while its senior pastor, his opponent Frederick Haynes, is on the ballot, and calls it a conflict of interest.
